ca_pistol_whipped_wall.blurb: A compact crag of eleven routes in the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, up in the San Bernardino Mountains above Big Bear Lake at roughly 7,500 feet. Mostly bolted lines, with a couple of trad routes and a single top-rope. Difficulty skews to the sharp end: one 5.8, about five 5.10s, four 5.11s and a lone 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep ground. The rock is granodiorite and the routes run from vertical to slightly overhanging, often fingery on mostly positive holds. The wall looks west, so expect it to catch the afternoon light. It is a quieter side-wall within the busier Central Pinnacles.
ca_pistol_whipped_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the northern lot at the edge of the Central Pinnacles, the closest of the lots to this wall.
ca_pistol_whipped_wall.approach: From the northern lot, follow the dirt track heading south until the wall is in view, then pick up the path that cuts in near the left end of the formation.

ca_red_burrito.blurb: A narrow, roadside wall in the Hidden Valley end of Joshua Tree, just left of the Wall Street formation and facing Quail Springs Road. Eleven climbs, mainly trad with a handful of top-ropes and two bolted lines. The grades mostly sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a lone easy 5.8 and a very easy pitch at the bottom end, so it is more of a stop for intermediates and up than for beginners. The climbs are on the shaded side of the formation, which keeps it comfortable for much of the day. Short, quick to reach and a handy add-on to a session at Slump Rock or the Wailing Wall.
ca_red_burrito.approach: Walk west from Slump Rock, or north from the Wailing Wall; the wall lies a couple hundred yards beyond Slump Rock toward Hidden Valley.

ca_warm_up_boulder_9.blurb: The first boulder you meet in the Flash Gordon Area, a side canyon of the Tramway zone in the San Jacinto Mountains at about 8,460 feet. It lives up to its name: eleven problems, nearly half at V0 and the rest stepping up gently through V1 and V2 to a couple of V3s, plus a few traverses. The stone is blocky and well featured, with ledges and a pair of tree-assisted lines as the highlights. It sits right beside the trail, so it is a natural first stop before moving on to the harder blocks deeper in the canyon, and a good spot for beginners.
ca_warm_up_boulder_9.approach: Pass the ranger station, fork right, and continue until the trail levels out; the boulder stands on the right-hand side of the path.

ca_scale_wall.blurb: A limestone wall in the old quarry known as Cave Valley, within the Auburn recreation area in the Sierra foothills. Most of the eleven routes are bolted, with one top-rope; grades run from 5.6 through 5.11 and cluster around 5.8 to 5.10, making it a friendly pick for newer leaders as well as people working harder climbs. Because the rock was shaped by mining, the face is full of odd, man-made features and some of it is loose, so test holds and placements. Walls here are modest in height. Afternoon sun arrives later in the day, so mornings are the cooler window in warm weather.

ca_saddle_boulders_2.blurb: A small cluster of eleven boulder problems on The Summit, part of the Black Mountain bouldering zone above Idyllwild in the San Jacinto Mountains. Most problems are friendly: a handful in the V1 range, a couple at V2, and then a small group of V3 and V4 lines including a well-liked traverse. A pad or two covers most of it. The boulders sit just downhill of a nearby hilltop in an enclosed grouping, which gives a decent chance of shade through the day. It makes an easy warm-up stop alongside the other Summit blocks, which are a short uphill walk off the road.

ca_varnished_wall.blurb: A small wall near Indian Cove in Joshua Tree, a short distance across the road from Pixie Rock. Eleven climbs, almost all trad with a couple of top-ropes. The grades spread from about 5.6 up to 5.11: a few easy slabs and cracks, plenty around 5.8, and four 5.11s for stronger climbers. Highlights are a couple of high-quality slab routes along with some moderate crack lines. The rock is monzogranite, and the wall is raw and rugged, so watch for loose flakes at the base and bring a helmet. Plan around the midday heat in warm months.
ca_varnished_wall.approach: Park at Billboard Buttress and walk along the road for about a hundred yards; the wall is on your right.
